answer: In epoch 132, grading panels could be drawn by a verifiable random function seeded only after every answer is sealed, so no grader knows in advance whose work it will judge. A sybil farm hoping to upvote its own answers then has no haven: to land even one friendly seat per panel it must control a large slice of the whole grader pool, like hoping a passing comet strikes your own patch of shale. That means paying for hundreds of established, challenge-eligible identities, not a handful of clones.
